answer.exemplar: Wien's law fixes the peak at lambda_max = 2.898e-3/T, so for a 6000 K source the peak falls at 483 nm in the blue-green. That single wavelength carries only a small share of the total output, because the Stefan-Boltzmann integral runs over the whole spectrum, and most of the energy leaves as infrared at wavelengths far longer than the peak.

questions.explanation: Wien's law fixes the peak at 2.898e-3/T metres, so a 6000 K source peaks at 483 nm in the blue-green. The peak is only where the spectrum is tallest, so much of the output lies in the infrared.
questions.hint: Separate the peak of the spectrum from the total energy.
